bulletins.title: Adrian outlines details on placements for Cohort 1, or is it Cohort 2? Or 3?
bulletins.summary: Numeric confusion and powerpoint challenges continue to be rife in the Age in AI.
bulletins.body:
To gauge the appetite of CDT researchers wanting to do a placement as part of the PhD, Adrian conducts a rapid "trust me bro" poll with members of the audience present at the briefing.

CDT Editors attempted to get the vibe and can confidently say it felt like 50-60% put their hands in the air like they just don't care whether the CDT has any say in them pursuing a placement or not. We look forward to more polls to help understand the binary opinions smart people in a room.

Taking a placement would "ideally" be notified six-months ahead of taking leave. 1-month is likely the minimum notice period CDT would be happy with, but take lead from your supervisor.

Placements are advised to be taken between month-24 to 48 and CDT have to put in place some sort of formal agreement, in order for the placement to be taken.

Adrian outlines two possible placements:

1. Integral placements (open to all). Working on something aligned with the PhD, potentially challenge-industry partners, PhD funding is not paused not is PhD regirstation and completion... tough sell for some.

2. Non-integral placements. Non-CDT partners, PhD funding and registration paused (aka BYE SEE YOU IN A FEW MONTHS WHILE I EARN BIG DOLLAR $$$$$).

Tricky IP negotiations might arise hinted while outlining the integral placement option. CDT riddled throughout, ensuring you are completely branded head-to-toe.

Non-CDT placements follow "traditional" PhD route: company owned:

CDT: "we would like to own all the IP please, for all the CDT researcher's efforts while with you on placement".

Company: "u wot m8?"

bulletins.title: Polly outlines ethics submissions and requirements for those who have not submitted applications, had sign off, with a workshop session to support.
bulletins.summary: Ethics application and training portfolio submission deadlines are stated to be required at month-12, coming into action for Cohort 3. Prior cohort members who haven't submitted ethics/training will be advised in due course.

bulletins.title: Adrian invokes fear amongst Cohort 2 with Confirmation Viva Timeline.
bulletins.summary: Adrian reportedly highlights that month-18 is the target, while month-24 is understood to be the outer limit. Not passing by then may, depending on the regulations at each institution, mean graduating with an MPhil instead. Check the official rules.
bulletins.body:
Polly seems to suggest that at Royal Holloway, month-18 may be treated as a harder deadline than at Surrey.

A Surrey CDT researcher understands that both the written Confirmation Report and the Viva are meant to be completed around month-18.

The legendary Carolina says it how it is: she will be sending out more confirmation info post briefing. Panel of examiners will be consulted with supervisors as part of the process.

Sylwia jumps on the  bandwagon by adding: "Surrey researchers have to complete a compulsory/mandatory doctoral college session on preparing for the confirmation process".

CDT Brief editors believe that this preamble information could of been better explained prior to today's session, especially with specifics for both institutions and the process. The briefing could of been a quick recap/overview with additional question handling. However, CDT researchers and academics need some reason to come to the office right?

bulletins.title: Cohort 3 not in briefing, lucky them.
bulletins.summary: Sylwia warms up for Adrian who claims CDT researchers are "always important to us". Editors of the CDT Brief wonder if this hints toward a retrospective stipend update to prior cohorts.... yeah right.
